transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-06-03 15:00 PDT
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Samir Rao (Redwood SE), Priya Khandelwal (Redwood Solutions), Maya Chen (ClearPath ML), Tom Alvarez (ClearPath Infra), Rina Patel (ClearPath PM), Ben Ortiz (ClearPath Security)

Summary:
Quick cadence sync on the pilot: discuss hedging multiple variant models, safe switchover strategy, rollback triggers, cost/latency tradeoffs, and next benchmarks. Customer wants clear escape hatch procedures and KMS/SOC2 compliance notes.

Topics:
1) Model variant hedging (A/B vs parallel hedging)
2) Pinning policy and freezepoints
3) Rollback / soft-fallback triggers and routing rules
4) Bench definitions for latency tail and token cost
5) Security/retention clarifications

Transcript body:
00:00 Alex (AE): okay team, thanks for joining. we wanna go over the variant hedging plan and the safe switchover. I put a short agenda in the invite.
00:12 Maya (ML): great, yeah we've been seeing some jitter on the 95th pct with the larger model and want to avoid user-visible regressions.
00:20 Samir (SE): mm-hmm, and to be clear—by hedging I mean running a lighter-weight variant in parallel and using routing to prefer the cheaper one unless quality drifts, right?
00:33 Maya (ML): correct. and also to capture metrics at inference time for quick rollback. we need to know what exact signals you recommend.
00:40 Samir (SE): good question. we typically track: rouge/semantic-match on a canned set, hallucination flags from the safety model, token delta, and 95th latency. also throughput per GPU. you probably wanna track both user-facing metrics and internal quality scores.
01:02 Tom (Infra): quick infra question — if we route to a fallback model on capacity fail, how disruptive is the KV cache state? i.e., can the fallback pick up the same context?
01:14 Samir (SE): there are two common patterns. soft fallback where we keep the same model family and the kv cache compatible — that needs same tokenizer and cache shape. hard fallback is to a smaller architecture; you lose kv compatibility and will warm a new cache, so expect a spike in latency for the first few requests.
01:35 Rina (PM): so for our UX, we need to avoid those warm spikes. what's your recommendation?
01:40 Samir (SE): do soft fallback when possible — model variants that are quantized or pruned but share the same architecture. also we can shadow-route a few percent to the fallback to keep the cache warm.
01:53 Ben (Security): on the security side, are there changes to data residency or retention when you route across regions or models? we need to be explicit for audits.
02:03 Alex (AE): good flag. Redwood can pin routing to region and to dedicated pools. we log every routing decision in the audit trail. i'll send the SOC2 snippet.
02:15 Ben (Security): I heard you say SOC2 but in the last doc there were only snippets; we need to confirm key management, HSM option, and if logs can be exported to our SIEM.
02:27 Priya (Solutions): yes, we support KMS integrations (AWS KMS/GCP CMEK) and can stream audit logs via secure syslog or push to a customer S3 with encryption. we'll attach the export example.
02:40 Maya (ML): on pinning policy, we want a way to freeze a version at a given timestamp so experiments don't drift. can you explain the freezepoint flow?
02:50 Samir (SE): sure — in Redwood you create a model pin which references a model version hash and optional quantization profile. you can set a freeze window where auto-rollouts are disabled; traffic is pinned until you unfreeze. rollbacks are a single-button operation that reassigns route to the earlier hash. important to test rollback in a low-traffic window though.
03:12 Alex (AE): and the playbook we've been using has a canary step, then 5% hedged shadow for 24h, then ramp. we also include a soft-gate: if 95th latency or quality deviates by threshold X we auto-fence.
03:30 Maya (ML): what are realistic thresholds?
03:33 Samir (SE): a starting rule is 95th latency +20% or quality drop > 3% on your eval set triggers a revert. but those numbers are tunable based on your tolerance.
03:47 Tom (Infra): for the bench we plan to run on our infra — do you want us to use your batching engine or replay real traffic?
03:55 Samir (SE): replaying production traffic is best for tail latency. we can provide a client harness and the request replayer. we'll also run a controlled bench using Redwood's batching to estimate per-token cost. link to bench script: https://drive.google.com/rw-bench (short).
04:12 Rina (PM): timeline — we aim to decide model variant by next week and start a 2-week pilot. is that feasible?
04:18 Alex (AE): yes, that's feasible. we can pin once you pick the primary and fallback variants.
04:24 Maya (ML): a few constraints: must be SSO, SAML into console, need audit retention for 12 months, and KMS with customer-managed keys. also we have a legal requirement to avoid sending PHI outside the VPC by default.
04:40 Ben (Security): yep, PHI rule is non-negotiable. we need a documented data flow.
04:45 Priya (Solutions): we have a private deployment plan — Redwood Private or Dedicated with VPC egress controls. we can scope that for the pilot; it changes pricing but keeps data inside your network.
04:57 Tom (Infra): price sensitivity though — we ran an RFP and village cloud/vertex looked cheaper at base but we need the ops guarantees.
05:06 Alex (AE): totally — tradeoff is predictable latency and integrated tooling. for the pilot we can do a small dedicated pool to keep costs bounded and measure unit economics.
05:17 Maya (ML): practical question: when you pin a model with a quantization profile, does that profile survive a rollback?
05:23 Samir (SE): yes, we version quantization profiles alongside the model bundle. rollback will restore both model hash and quant profile. small caveat: if you rollback to an unquantized model you'll have different token costs.
05:36 Rina (PM): ok let's recap actions before we run out of time.
05:40 Alex (AE): recap — Redwood: send playbook + SOC2/KMS note + bench harness. Samir: share runbook and safe-switchover steps. Customer: upload prompts, confirm retention/KMS, and pick variants.
05:56 Maya (ML): we'll try to pick the primary and at least two fallback variants — one architecture-matching (soft fallback) and one cheaper but different (hard fallback).
06:05 Ben (Security): i'll review the SOC2 snippets and get back with any gaps.
06:10 Tom (Infra): can we schedule the bench on Thursday 06/04 at 10am our time?
06:15 Samir (SE): yes — that works for me, i'll bring the replayer config.
06:20 Alex (AE): perfect. i'll send meeting invite and the pricing sketch.
